transcript:
This message comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled pros
to get their home projects done well for over 30 years. For everything from minor repairs
to major remodels, find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman. Seven senators are calling on President Trump to
reverse course on his diesel deal with Russia. As NPR's Luke Garrett reports, the bipartisan
group says Trump's agreement is illegal. On Friday, Trump shocked lawmakers when he
announced the deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump said the agreement
would immediately supply U.S. and international markets with hundreds of thousands of tons of
diesel. On Sunday, three Democrats and four Republicans said Trump's deal is illegal
because Congress "explicitly banned Russian energy imports" in 2022. Here's GOP Senator
Tom Tillis on NBC News. I do believe there's a legitimate case for saying the president's
not following the law. We were very clear that Russia is the aggressor. Russia is the one who
can end this war by backing out of territory that they occupied. The seven senators called
on Trump to "immediately reverse course" on his oil deal with Russia. Following the war with Iran,
the high cost of gas has hurt Trump politically. Luke Garrett, NPR News, Washington.
A passenger terminal at the international airport in Riyadh was hit again on Sunday. The attack came
just one day after a missile hit the complex and killed 13 people. The Saudis are blaming the
attacks on Houthi rebels in Yemen. Democratic Senator Chris Murphy of Connecticut has just
returned from Saudi Arabia. He says the U.S. should not get involved. I don't think the United States
should go to war in Yemen. I mean, this administration is absolutely incompetent
in war making. And so just as we have made the Middle East worse and more chaotic by getting
involved in a war against Iran, we would simply escalate and make the situation even more dangerous
if we then went to war not only with Iran but with the Houthis in Yemen as well. Murphy was speaking
Sunday on CBS's Face the Nation news program. Mexico's West Coast is being pounded by a
Category 3 hurricane, as NPR's Ada Peralta reports. It's already bringing torrential rain and dangerous
winds. The good news is that Hurricane Simon is expected to skirt the coast and will likely not
directly hit the bigger cities along its path. Still, Colima and Puerto Vallarta are reporting
strong winds, heavy surf, and flooding. Mexican President Claudia Shambaugh has ordered citizens
in four different municipalities to shelter in place until the danger has passed. Shambaugh has
also deployed the military in those areas to help with recovery. The National Hurricane
Center expects Hurricane Simon to weaken in the coming hours and then continue moving along the
coast. Simon is forecast to make landfall on Wednesday near Masatlan. Forecasters say it will
likely be a tropical storm by then. Ada Peralta, NPR News, Mexico City. A federal judge Sunday
ordered President Trump to end airing television commercials paid for with federal money.
Trump has been airing commercials that promote his political views. A coalition of groups had
challenged the ads, saying they were an illegal use of government funds. You're listening to NPR News.
In Asia, stocks fell Monday ahead of the earnings season as investors worried about massive AI
spending and lagging returns. A new study finds that younger and lower-income women who were
diagnosed with breast cancer tend to see delays in care, NPR's Yuki Naguchi reports.
Women under age 40 are not typically screened for breast cancer and may face potential biases in
treatment if they have the disease because of their youth. In a study published in the
journal Cancer, investigators looked at data to identify the wait time for care among a thousand
individuals diagnosed with breast cancer enrolled in the young women's breast cancer study. It found
153 instances of patients, particularly those who are lower income, facing delays of three months or
more to see a clinician about their symptoms. Younger patients were likely to see treatment
delayed by two months or more. The report says the delays may not have led to the need for more
treatment but did not affect overall survival. Yuki Naguchi, NPR News. Pope Leo says he'll undergo
surgery in the next few days to remove a nodular lesion on his lung. He says the lesion was
discovered at an early stage and is well localized. The recovery time is expected to last a week. The
71-year-old Pont have made the announcement during his Sunday blessing. It is his first
major health event since becoming Pope 17 months ago. At least 139 migrants, including 15 children,
have died after a boat with 305 people on board collapsed off the coast of Djibouti in Africa.
The boat was traveling to Yemen when it capsized. At least 84 people remain missing. It's one of the
deadliest shipwrecks to occur on the popular route, which takes people to Gulf states in
search of well-paying jobs. I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: Seven senators urge Trump to reverse his diesel deal with Russia, calling it illegal
Passenger terminal at Riyadh international airport hit again, one day after deadly missile attack
Senator Chris Murphy says U.S. should not go to war in Yemen against Houthis
Hurricane Simon pounds Mexico's West Coast, with Colima and Puerto Vallarta reporting strong winds and flooding
Federal judge orders Trump to stop airing TV ads paid for with federal money
Asian stocks fall ahead of earnings season over AI spending and lagging returns
Study finds younger, lower-income women with breast cancer face delays in care
Pope Leo to undergo surgery to remove a lung lesion discovered at an early stage
At least 139 migrants dead after boat capsizes off Djibouti bound for Yemen
